findings.message: The `row could not be built` case does not isolate its cause, and nothing tests the actual fix in report.sh. The old `${j:-\{\}}` expanded to the literal `\{\}` whenever `status_job` printed nothing. That made `--argjson j` fail, so every dispatched or running change with no job output got a `?` row with the note `row could not be built`. The new test uses a dispatched record, so `status_job` runs, and then asserts that same note. It would pass with the old code for that reason alone, without `agent_started:5` having any effect. No case asserts that a dispatched change with empty `status_job` output now gets a normal, non-`?` row. That assertion is the one that fails without the `[[ -n "$j" ]] || j='{}'` fix. Add a table case for dispatched and running records whose `status_job` stub prints nothing, and assert the row's state is not `?`. Give the `row could not be built` case a failure that does not depend on `j`, such as a stub `status_job` that prints valid `{}`, and assert that the record shape alone triggers the note. Also check that the other `--argjson` inputs (`r`, `p`, `b`) are normalised the same way, since an empty `b` from a failed `api_obj` gives the same failure.
findings.scenario: A dispatched change whose `status_job` prints nothing. Before the fix, the row was `?` with note `row could not be built`. After the fix, it is a normal row. The added test uses a dispatched record and expects the `?` note, so it is green for the old bug too and proves nothing about the fix. Reverting the `j` default leaves the new tests green.
